metadata.description: Source SBL for the 56 interior pages of IAKESI Chapter 4. Cover production is separate and excluded.

production_policy.scope: interior pages only; cover production is separate
production_policy.print_target: Amazon KDP Premium Color paperback, 6 x 9 inch final trim
production_policy.style: full-color realistic manga within the established IAKESI visual language
production_policy.zoran_ears: normal rounded human ears; never pointed or elven
production_policy.old_chapter_pdf: blocking and spatial reference only; do not copy its overly dark exposure or panel layouts
production_policy.color: RGB working images composed for CMYK-safe conversion; preserve readable midtones and shadow detail
production_policy.safe_area: faces, lettering space, important hands, essential props, and critical action remain inside the page safe rectangle
production_policy.art_layer: artwork only; no dialogue, narration, balloons, tails, folios, panel numbers, or production metadata
production_policy.lettering_layer: transparent RGBA placement guide registered exactly to the art layer
production_policy.text_authority: the page TXT file is authoritative for exact reader-visible wording and punctuation
production_policy.reading_order: left-to-right and top-to-bottom unless a page explicitly states otherwise
production_policy.forbidden_symbol: never invent a generic multi-point star or compass emblem
production_policy.external_600dpi_pipeline: upscale 1024x1536 to 3700x5550, then crop 25 pixels from the binding side to 3675x5550
production_policy.dream_sequence: Pages 15-26 are a dream or vision; Zorna may be radiant but must retain readable facial and costume detail
production_policy.magic: keep magic visually legible and consistent; do not obscure the caster's face or physical action unless explicitly required
production_policy.population_realism: anonymous populations must be varied and plausible rather than uniformly idealized

He smiles as the technique finally succeeds.

narration.content: Schools and teachers carried the new spells from city to city.
In workshops and marketplaces, neighbors practiced together.
Each group shared what it discovered.
What began as one man’s revelation spread through formal study and everyday cooperation.
